standards.title: Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems
PostgreSQL High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication

skip_groups.reason: The isolated generic Windows test job deliberately does not start Ultra Server on localhost:7777.
skip_groups.substitute: The same live contract tests run against a started Ultra Server in the dedicated Windows live-contract job and against the production PostgreSQL-backed job.
skip_groups.non_equivalence: A skip in the generic job is not itself evidence; only the dedicated jobs' real executions support the live-contract claims.
skip_groups.closure: Keep every node ID and skip reason allowlisted, and require the dedicated live jobs to pass on the exact commit.

skip_groups.reason: Windows cannot execute POSIX owner, mode, no-follow symlink, and replace-open-file semantics.
skip_groups.substitute: The four exact skipped node IDs run without skips in the dedicated ubuntu-latest POSIX runtime-ownership job.
skip_groups.non_equivalence: Windows DACL, reparse-point, and handle-retarget tests remain separate because POSIX results do not prove Windows semantics and Windows results do not prove POSIX semantics.
skip_groups.closure: Keep the dedicated POSIX and Windows-native tests green on the exact commit.

ci_receipts.scope: PR 50 exact-head two-host Spark acceptance and full repository matrix
Post-merge master full matrix including live Ultra, production durability, and final HA acceptance
Post-merge master exact BPC/TSK Enterprise B-to-A failback, stale-B denial, and full six-PostgreSQL plus Redis quorum/Sentinel matrix
PR 67 exact-head repeated same-principal recovery, stale-site resynchronization, 15 restarted no-effect probes, and full six-PostgreSQL plus Redis quorum/Sentinel matrix
PR 68 exact-head post-partition-heal BPC/TSK stale-writer denial, 25 total restarted no-effect probes, and full six-PostgreSQL plus Redis quorum/Sentinel matrix

levels.requirement: Interrupt live cutover processes before and after durable boundaries and resume without torn or duplicate state.
levels.limitations: Pass applies to the named child-process and database-process faults, not loss of an operating-system host.

levels.requirement: Lose and restart the promoted PostgreSQL process and verify identity, readiness, and committed authority state.
levels.limitations: This is PostgreSQL process/container loss and restart, not destruction of the host or storage volume.

levels.requirement: Crash and isolate the active Redis master; require quorum promotion, monotonic fencing, old-master denial, and convergence after heal.
levels.limitations: All three Redis data nodes and Sentinels ran on one hosted runner, so this proves failover semantics but not independent infrastructure failure domains.

levels.requirement: Place at least three Sentinel instances on computers or virtual machines expected to fail independently.
levels.limitations: The hosted quorum uses separate containers on one runner; Spark-1/Spark-2 currently provide only two physical hosts and the Spark-2 Redis target is not a quorum member.
levels.closure: Provision a third independent host or VM failure domain, distribute Redis/Sentinel members, then repeat crash, partition, heal, rollback, and monotonic-epoch drills.

levels.requirement: Execute the governed TSK A-to-B-to-A lifecycle on distinct admitted physical hosts with independent PostgreSQL state authorities.
levels.limitations: Spark-1 and Spark-2 are on the same LAN. Source and control PostgreSQL authorities share Spark-1.

levels.requirement: Disrupt the live inter-host target service path, prove fail-closed behavior with no evidence artifact, heal, and reconverge.
levels.limitations: The real service path was disconnected and refused the run; heal reached PostgreSQL in 557 ms and the full handoff completed in 33942 ms. The fault transcript is operator-observed rather than a committed machine-produced fault receipt, and this is not loss of the host network or LAN.
levels.closure: Automate the disconnect/refusal/no-receipt/heal sequence with write-once secret-free evidence and independent review; separately execute a network-domain/site isolation test on suitable infrastructure.

levels.requirement: Interrupt an entire admitted authority host and recover or fail over without relying on processes that remain alive on that host.
levels.limitations: Spark-2 hosts unrelated owner workloads. Stopping its acceptance PostgreSQL or network does not equal power loss or chassis loss, and those substitutes are not presented as equivalent.
levels.closure: Move the acceptance target to a dedicated host or obtain an approved maintenance window, then power off or hard-reset that host and retain measured recovery evidence.

levels.requirement: Test recovery and operations at an alternate processing site separated from the primary site hazards.
levels.limitations: Both Sparks are on the same LAN and no independent geography, power, or network provider is admitted. Containers, VMs, and port blocks on this LAN cannot prove a site boundary.
levels.closure: Provision an actual alternate site or cloud region with independent power/network, admit its identities, and run full interruption, recovery, failback, and accessibility exercises there.

levels.requirement: Couple each authoritative BPC pair, TSK credential, identity-binding, idempotency, and applicable nonce mutation to its durable replication transaction, then compose the cross-authority handoff through exact signed receipts.
levels.limitations: Pass is bounded to the signed snapshot-after-fence saga on the named six-PostgreSQL plus Redis quorum/Sentinel topology. Each authority commits through its own reviewed transaction and exact signed receipt; this is not a claim of simultaneous cross-database atomic commit.

levels.requirement: Strip secrets from replicated state and require a separately authorized target credential unseal or reprovisioning ceremony before readiness.
levels.limitations: Real PostgreSQL tests prove redacted export and fresh target credential reprovisioning, but no controlled production key-custody/unseal ceremony with independent operator authorization has been executed and retained.
levels.closure: Execute the production custody ceremony using separately controlled identities, prove readiness refusal before reprovisioning, retain only secret-free evidence, and independently review the result.

levels.requirement: Deny stale, replayed, tampered, gapped, and rolled-back replicas before promotion, readiness, or mutation.
levels.limitations: Pass is bounded to the signed component and Enterprise state formats and the named hosted topology; it is not evidence for an untested storage or site implementation.

levels.requirement: Keep the prior writer fenced through restart and partition healing, including the Enterprise completed-authority path.
levels.limitations: Twenty-five distinct restarted processes cover BPC, TSK, and Enterprise at all five cuts. BPC and TSK are denied both before and after the real Redis partition/heal; Enterprise probes run after heal. Every probe requires protocol-specific typed denial and an unchanged exact-authority digest. Evidence is one-host container/process topology and does not claim destroyed physical-site or catastrophic source-volume-loss recovery.

levels.requirement: Reconcile a recovered old authority and prevent it from writing until full verified convergence under a newer epoch.
levels.limitations: The hosted six-PostgreSQL plus Redis/Sentinel drill reuses the stale B PostgreSQL authorities, proves stale writes have no committed effect, imports and independently attests BPC/TSK/Enterprise state, and permits only the exact first new-epoch mutations. This is process/container and logical-authority recovery on one CI host, not recovery from destroyed physical storage or a multi-site disaster.

levels.requirement: Recover the system to a known state, validate integrity, and resume governed operations.
levels.limitations: The drill performs signed Enterprise-state rebuild and exact PostgreSQL restart on the promoted authority. It does not restore a full deployment from independent backups at an alternate site.
levels.closure: Restore PostgreSQL, Redis policy state, identity recovery material, and provenance evidence into an isolated independent deployment; validate all authority identities and record recovery point/time.

levels.requirement: Restore protected backups into an isolated environment and verify application, identity, transaction, and evidence continuity.
levels.limitations: A reviewed runbook exists, but no retained artifact proves the complete isolated backup restore procedure has run end to end.
levels.closure: Run the documented isolated restore using real backup media and separate recovery identities; retain secret-free hashes, RPO/RTO, integrity results, and destruction evidence.

levels.requirement: Return Enterprise-owned identity, idempotency, nonce, and credential-binding authority from B to A under a new epoch while the old B writer remains fenced.
levels.limitations: One exact A-to-B-to-A Enterprise cycle passes on the named topology with completed BPC/TSK artifacts, terminal source fencing, independently countersigned state, fresh target credential reprovisioning, stale-B protocol and completion denial, idempotent retry, and measured data-loss RPO zero. Repeated cycles, host/site loss, and production custody remain separate matrix levels.

levels.requirement: Repeat primary/replica failover and failback while preserving the same bound principal and monotonically advancing authority.
levels.limitations: Two complete A-to-B-to-A cycles plus an exact stale-B rebuild and governed A-to-B recovery pass under pinned BPC and TSK authorities on six distinct PostgreSQL systems plus real Redis. Twenty-five distinct restarted processes cover BPC, TSK, and Enterprise at all five cuts; BPC and TSK are denied again after the real Redis partition/heal and Enterprise probes run after heal. Each probe requires a protocol-specific typed denial and an unchanged exact-authority digest, so an error after a committed effect cannot count as a pass. Evidence remains process/container and logical-authority recovery on one CI host, not destroyed physical-site recovery.

levels.requirement: Detect, alert, and retain operator-visible evidence for authority loss, replication lag, denied promotion, stale writers, and recovery failure.
levels.limitations: Monitoring configuration and security tests pass, but an independently observed deployment alerting drill for the exact multi-host topology has not run.
levels.closure: Deploy the approved monitors and alert routes, inject each named fault, prove timely delivery and acknowledgement, and retain bounded incident evidence.

levels.requirement: Retain acceptance and incident evidence in an immutable or equivalently governed store outside the faulted system.
levels.limitations: A real S3 Object Lock COMPLIANCE-mode run proved remote retention, readback, stable seal indexing, and conflicting-root rejection. The exact HA acceptance and incident artifacts are not yet routed through that sink, and ongoing custody/legal-hold operations are not established.
levels.closure: Route the exact HA acceptance and incident artifacts into the reviewed immutable sink, then exercise retention/deletion denial, recovery access, and continuing custody operations.

levels.requirement: Protect signing, recovery, and reprovisioning keys with reviewed separation, rotation, revocation, backup, and recovery controls.
levels.limitations: The code enforces separate key roles and rejects private material in verifier paths, but the acceptance topology uses file-held test keys rather than an independently operated HSM/TPM custody service and ceremony.
levels.closure: Provision production custody identities, exercise rotation/revocation/recovery with dual control, and retain non-secret attestation and audit evidence.

levels.requirement: Obtain independent security review of the exact deployment topology and its retained evidence, not only source components.
levels.limitations: PR 50 received independent adversarial review of the exact two-host TSK slice. The complete Enterprise/BPC/TSK/Redis/restore topology has not received an independent deployment review.
levels.closure: After the full topology and remaining drills exist, provide its manifests, receipts, custody boundary, and failure evidence to an independent reviewer and resolve all findings.

levels.requirement: Measure recovery outcomes and compare them with approved recovery point and recovery time objectives.
levels.limitations: The tests measure RPO/RTO or elapsed time for named faults, but no owner-approved business impact analysis or production SLO defines the required targets. Asynchronous or catastrophic source-storage loss is not claimed as RPO zero.
levels.closure: Approve workload-specific RPO/RTO targets, encode technical acceptance thresholds, and demonstrate them across process, database, Redis, host, network, restore, and alternate-site exercises.

levels.requirement: Coordinate contingency testing with related organizational plans and responsible roles rather than exercising the technical system in isolation.
levels.limitations: Repository runbooks and tests do not prove coordination with business continuity, incident response, crisis communications, or external service-provider plans.
levels.closure: Name plan owners and dependencies, conduct a coordinated exercise, retain approvals and observations, and feed corrective actions back into each affected plan.

levels.requirement: Use automation to execute contingency tests, collect results, and prevent unevidenced success claims where technically feasible.
levels.limitations: Hosted component and two-host handoff tests are automated, but the cross-host partition was operator-driven and whole-host, alternate-site, restore, alerting, and custody exercises are not automated.
levels.closure: Automate all safe fault and evidence steps; for destructive or operator-controlled steps, automate admission, timestamps, assertions, receipt creation, and post-condition verification.

levels.requirement: Exercise self-challenge and adversarial scenarios that attempt to invalidate contingency assumptions and success signals.
levels.limitations: Tamper, replay, rollback, gap, split-brain, crash, and false-success paths are challenged in CI, but the full alternate-site, custody, monitoring, restore, and human-response assumptions have not been independently challenged.
levels.closure: Run a controlled red-team/tabletop exercise against the complete topology and operational plans, including false telemetry, partial restore, credential loss, delayed detection, and failed alternate-site access.

levels.requirement: Execute database-dependent Ultra integration tests with real PostgreSQL rather than treating local skips as passing evidence.
levels.limitations: The generic Windows suite has 38 explicit environment/OS skips. The authoritative production job separately ran the database-dependent Ultra suite 65/65, independent-state suite 2/2, and Ultra outbox suite 1/1 with zero skips; no claim is made that the entire Python suite has zero skips.
